regulatory_status: Each component FDA-approved decades ago: irinotecan (Camptosar, 1996), 5-FU (1962), leucovorin (1952). All generic; FOLFIRI is a generic combination regimen.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 first-line preferred regimen for metastatic colorectal cancer (NCCN Colon Cancer v3.2026). Patient is on this now.

manufacturer.company: Multiple generic manufacturers (Hospira/Pfizer, Sandoz, Teva, Fresenius Kabi, Sun)
manufacturer.notes: Irinotecan reference label is Pfizer's Camptosar; 5-FU and leucovorin have no single reference brand. Sourced from any oncology pharmacy.

payer_access_notes: Universal Medicare / commercial coverage as a first-line CRC regimen. No prior auth typically needed beyond standard chemo billing. UGT1A1 *28/*28 carriers warrant a starting-dose reduction per the irinotecan label.
access_summary: FOLFIRI is the regimen the patient is currently receiving; access is fully routine. The peri-HIPEC sequencing question matters more than the access question: most centers complete 4-6 cycles, restage, and operate during a 3-6 week washout.
next_steps: Confirm UGT1A1 *28 genotype and DPYD status before any dose change (target_validation has these as essential rows).
Coordinate the systemic-to-surgical handoff with the HIPEC surgeon so the last irinotecan dose lands at least 3 weeks before CRS to limit perioperative neutropenia.
notes: BICC-C established FOLFIRI as the irinotecan-backbone reference. Routine first-line option in mCRC.

regulatory_status: Component drugs all FDA-approved. The FOLFOXIRI combination is a published regimen rather than a labeled product; bevacizumab is on-label as a first-line mCRC combination partner (Avastin label).
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 first-line option for patients with good performance status, especially with high tumor burden, peritoneal disease, or interest in cytoreduction.

trials.title: CAIRO6: perioperative systemic chemo + CRS-HIPEC vs CRS-HIPEC alone
trials.notes: Tests perioperative FOLFOX or FOLFOXIRI ± bevacizumab around CRS-HIPEC. Closed to new enrollment but the protocol template is exactly the patient's pathway.

manufacturer.notes: FOLFOXIRI components all generic. Bevacizumab is the on-label biologic in the regimen; Avastin / biosimilars Mvasi (Amgen) and Zirabev (Pfizer) are routinely substituted.

payer_access_notes: Standard coverage. TRIBE / TRIBE2 are the registrational evidence for adding oxaliplatin and irinotecan together in 1L; routinely approved for younger fit patients with peritoneal-dominant or high-tumor-burden disease.
access_summary: An intensification option if the team wants to expand the regimen from FOLFIRI + bev to triplet + bev before CRS-HIPEC. Coverage is routine; the operational decision is tolerability and the peri-operative window, not access.
next_steps: Reassess whether triplet intensification is wanted given the patient is already tolerating FOLFIRI-bev. CAIRO6 is the protocol-shaped template even though it is closed to new enrollment.
If switching, confirm oxaliplatin-naive status (the prior-therapy list shows FOLFIRI only) and lay in a neuropathy plan.
notes: TRIBE / TRIBE2 anchor the evidence base. CAIRO6 is the cleanest peritoneal-spread protocol template even though new enrollment is closed.

regulatory_status: Oxaliplatin FDA-approved 2002; 5-FU, leucovorin, bevacizumab approved; biosimilar bevacizumab options Mvasi / Zirabev approved.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 first-line preferred regimen for mCRC. Equivalent efficacy to FOLFIRI-bev in MAVERICC.

manufacturer.company: Sanofi (Eloxatin reference) + generic oxaliplatin makers; Genentech/Roche bevacizumab

payer_access_notes: Universal first-line coverage. No prior-auth obstacles.
access_summary: Alternative first-line backbone if FOLFIRI is paused before the HIPEC window or if a different toxicity profile is wanted. Cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy is the practical limiting factor; the patient has not been exposed to oxaliplatin yet, so this lane is preserved.
next_steps: Bank FOLFOX as the post-HIPEC adjuvant option since the patient is oxaliplatin-naive — saves the cleaner second-line drug for the moment it is most needed.
notes: MAVERICC and Stein et al. established equivalence between FOLFOX-bev and FOLFIRI-bev in 1L mCRC.

intervention_label: Bevacizumab (Avastin) and biosimilars (Mvasi, Zirabev, Vegzelma, Alymsys, Abevmy, Aybintio)
regulatory_status: FDA-approved 2004 for first- and second-line mCRC in combination with fluoropyrimidine-based chemo. Multiple biosimilars approved (Mvasi 2017, Zirabev 2019, Vegzelma 2022, Alymsys 2022, Aybintio 2022, Abevmy 2024). EMA-approved with comparable wording.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 component of first- and second-line mCRC regimens. Currently in the patient's regimen.

manufacturer.company: Genentech/Roche (Avastin); Amgen (Mvasi); Pfizer (Zirabev); Celltrion (Vegzelma); Amneal (Alymsys); Samsung Bioepis (Aybintio); Biocon Biologics/Viatris (Abevmy)
manufacturer.notes: Genentech routes mCRC inquiries through Avastin Access Solutions: 1-866-422-2377. Biosimilar substitution is plan-driven; clinical equivalence is established.

payer_access_notes: Routine Medicare and commercial coverage as a first-line CRC biologic. Many plans now mandate biosimilar substitution.
access_summary: Active component of the patient's regimen. Hold bevacizumab 4-6 weeks before cytoreductive surgery to limit wound-healing complications; resume 4-6 weeks after surgery once healing is complete.
next_steps: Coordinate the bevacizumab pause with the CRS-HIPEC team: last dose at least 4 weeks before surgery, ideally 6, and no restart until the abdominal wound is healed.
If the plan switches the patient to a biosimilar mid-line, document the brand for ctDNA-MRD interpretation continuity.
notes: Bevacizumab is the on-label antiangiogenic in the patient's current regimen. Sequencing around HIPEC is the only practical access question.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved August 2012 (VELOUR) for metastatic CRC progressing after oxaliplatin, in combination with FOLFIRI. EMA-approved with comparable wording.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 second-line option in combination with FOLFIRI after oxaliplatin failure.

manufacturer.company: Regeneron / Sanofi (Sanofi handles oncology marketing as Zaltrap)
manufacturer.notes: Sanofi US medical information 1-800-633-1610 handles Zaltrap. Distinct from Eylea HD which is the ophthalmic formulation.

payer_access_notes: On-label in second line after oxaliplatin. The patient has not had oxaliplatin yet, so the labeled sequence does not apply unless they advance to triplet-then-aflibercept later. Off-label use as a bevacizumab alternative in 1L is not standard.
access_summary: Approved, labeled second-line option after FOLFOX/oxaliplatin failure. The patient is oxaliplatin-naive on FOLFIRI-bev, so aflibercept fits the second-line slot only after a future FOLFOX leg.
next_steps: Park aflibercept as a labeled second-line antiangiogenic if the patient eventually switches to FOLFOX and progresses; not in immediate scope while FOLFIRI-bev is active.
notes: VELOUR is the registrational evidence. Sequence-dependent fit.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved April 2015 (RAISE) for second-line mCRC in combination with FOLFIRI after bevacizumab + oxaliplatin + fluoropyrimidine. EMA-approved with similar wording.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 second-line option (FOLFIRI + ramucirumab) after first-line bev-containing oxaliplatin regimens.

manufacturer.notes: Lilly Medical Information operates 1-800-LillyRx for HCP queries. Expanded-access is case-by-case.

payer_access_notes: Labeled second-line use; routine Medicare coverage. Same patient-specific caveat as aflibercept: the FOLFIRI partner is on-label but RAISE enrolled patients post-FOLFOX-bev.
access_summary: Approved second-line antiangiogenic. RAISE specifically tested it after FOLFOX-bev, so its label is sequence-dependent. The patient is on FOLFIRI-bev in 1L, so ramucirumab fits the second-line slot if they advance through oxaliplatin first.
next_steps: Hold as a sequence option for 2L+ after oxaliplatin exposure. No immediate action.
notes: RAISE registrational. Comparable to aflibercept on hazard ratio.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved 2004 for KRAS wild-type, EGFR-expressing mCRC (left-sided preferred). The FDA label explicitly excludes KRAS-mutant tumors based on extended-RAS analyses (CRYSTAL, FIRE-3, CALGB/SWOG 80405). EMA-approved with similar exclusion.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 for RAS wild-type, BRAF wild-type, left-sided mCRC in first and later lines. NCCN treats codon 59 mutations as resistance variants alongside the canonical exon 2/3/4 KRAS hotspots.

trials.title: RMC-GI-102: RAS(ON) inhibitors + cetuximab / chemo platform
trials.indication: RAS-mutant GI tumors (atypical KRAS arms include A59)
trials.notes: The daraxonrasib + cetuximab combination arms in RMC-GI-102 may treat A59T as eligible under the broader 'non-G12C RAS' bucket; sponsor confirmation is the gate. This is the only realistic A59T-eligible context where cetuximab moves back onto the table.

manufacturer.company: Eli Lilly (ImClone Systems / Bristol-Myers Squibb originally)

payer_access_notes: Off-label in any RAS-mutant tumor including atypical alleles. Payer denial is essentially universal unless a panitumumab-A59T case-report precedent (pmid:30538852) is cited and the team obtains a medical-exception with sponsor or trial coverage. The cleanest payer-supported access is via the daraxonrasib + cetuximab arm of RMC-GI-102, where the sponsor covers cetuximab.
access_summary: Off-label for this patient because A59T is treated as a RAS-pathway-activating mutation by current guideline consensus. A single 2018 case report (Mavroudis et al., panitumumab in KRAS A59T mCRC) is the entire body of clinical-response data for atypical KRAS responses to anti-EGFR, and the consensus-fit answer is to not use cetuximab off-label in this allele. The clean route into cetuximab is the RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062) daraxonrasib + cetuximab combination arm where the sponsor pays.
next_steps: Treat single-agent or chemo-combination cetuximab as off the table outside a trial; do not bet payer effort on the panitumumab case-report precedent.
If the team wants cetuximab in the regimen, route the patient toward RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062) and ask Revolution Medicines whether A59T is accepted in the daraxonrasib + cetuximab arm.
geographic_scope: Universal availability; off-label in this allele.
notes: FIRE-3 and CALGB/SWOG 80405 anchor the RAS-wild-type cetuximab evidence. A59T is treated as a resistance variant by NCCN.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved 2006 for KRAS wild-type mCRC. Label updated 2014 to include extended-RAS wild-type. EMA-approved with similar wording.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 for RAS wild-type, BRAF wild-type, left-sided mCRC. KRAS A59T treated as a resistance variant alongside the canonical hotspots; not a labeled-eligible allele.

manufacturer.notes: Amgen Medical Information operates 1-800-77-AMGEN for HCP queries. Amgen Assist 360 handles patient access at 1-888-427-7478.

payer_access_notes: Off-label in atypical-RAS tumors. The single supportive case is Mavroudis et al. 2018 (pmid:30538852), which reported a panitumumab-FOLFIRI response in a KRAS A59T-mutant patient. Off-label exception requests can cite this single report but most payers decline. Amgen Assist 360 cannot help unless the patient is on-label.
access_summary: Off-label for A59T-mutant disease. One published case report (Mavroudis et al. 2018) is the only direct evidence that an A59T tumor can respond to anti-EGFR. The clean defensive call is to treat anti-EGFR as off the table for this allele; the team can revisit if the A59T VAF is low and a clonal sub-population looks RAS-wild-type on plasma.
next_steps: Confirm the KRAS A59T VAF and that the rest of the extended RAS panel (KRAS exon 2/3/4, NRAS, HRAS) and BRAF V600 are wild-type before any anti-EGFR conversation.
If the VAF is low and the rest of the panel is clean, run the Mavroudis case report past the patient's payer for a medical-exception request, with the understanding that approval is unlikely.
If pursued, Amgen Medical Information (1-800-77-AMGEN) can supply the labeled prescribing information packet but does not advocate for off-label use.
geographic_scope: Universal availability; off-label in this allele.
notes: The Mavroudis et al. 2018 case report is the only published clinical-response data point in KRAS A59T. NCCN treats codon 59 mutations as anti-EGFR resistance variants.

intervention_label: Anti-EGFR mAbs (cetuximab / panitumumab) in extended-RAS-mutant mCRC — evidence-summary entry
regulatory_status: Composite category; see cetuximab and panitumumab rows.
guideline_status: Atypical RAS alleles (including codon 59) are treated as anti-EGFR resistance variants in NCCN v3.2026 and ESMO 2025. Single case reports are not guideline-supported.

manufacturer.notes: See cetuximab and panitumumab rows for direct contact information.

payer_access_notes: Off-label in atypical KRAS alleles. The collected evidence (meta-analysis Sorich et al., De Roock et al., case reports) supports treating extended-RAS-mutant tumors as anti-EGFR resistant rather than sensitive.
access_summary: Aggregated row for the cetuximab/panitumumab + atypical-KRAS evidence base. Bottom line: treat anti-EGFR as off the table for KRAS A59T outside a sponsor-coverage trial (RMC-GI-102) or a documented medical-exception with a low-VAF rationale.
next_steps: Use the cetuximab and panitumumab rows for operational decisions; this row captures the meta-evidence summary.
notes: Meta-analysis and retrospective cohorts (Sorich, De Roock, Bando, Cremolini) anchor the resistance call. The single 2018 case report is the dissenting datum.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved November 8, 2023 (FRESCO-2) for previously treated metastatic CRC after fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, anti-VEGF, and (if RAS-WT) anti-EGFR therapy. EMA-approved June 2024.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 third-line+ option for mCRC after standard chemo and biologic exposure.

trials.notes: China-only sites; not accessible to a US-based patient.

manufacturer.notes: Takeda Oncology Medical Information operates 1-844-662-8532. Patient support: Takeda Oncology Here2Assist at 1-844-817-6468.

payer_access_notes: Routine third-line coverage. Will become relevant for this patient only after at least 2 prior lines (FOLFIRI-bev, then FOLFOX or another biologic). Manageable hypertension is the main toxicity gating; bevacizumab co-administration is not standard.
access_summary: Approved 3L+ option. The patient is still 1L on FOLFIRI-bev so fruquintinib is not yet in scope, but bank it as a labeled third-line lane.
next_steps: Reserve fruquintinib as the post-FOLFOX, post-bevacizumab labeled antiangiogenic for 3L use.
If the patient eventually reaches 3L, Takeda's Here2Assist (1-844-817-6468) handles benefits investigations and copay support.
geographic_scope: US, EU, UK, AU available; China-specific trials are domestic.
notes: FRESCO-2 was the registrational global trial; FRESCO was the China-only precursor.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved 2012 for refractory mCRC. ReDOS dose-escalation (80→120→160 mg) is the operational standard.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 third-line+ option, with ReDOS escalation noted as a tolerability framework.

trials.title: Botensilimab + balstilimab + regorafenib (City of Hope)
trials.notes: Closed to new enrollment. PI Marwan Fakih at City of Hope. Not enrollable today.

payer_access_notes: Routine 3L+ coverage. ReDOS dosing is increasingly the default to manage hand-foot-skin reaction.
access_summary: Approved 3L+ option, will become operationally relevant later in the disease course. Same as fruquintinib: not in scope until the patient progresses past 2L.
next_steps: Bank as a 3L+ antiangiogenic. REGONIVO (regorafenib + nivolumab) is the MSS-CRC immune-combination precedent but did not move the needle in confirmatory trials.
notes: CORRECT and CONCUR were the registrational trials. ReDOS established the dose-escalation framework.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved September 2015 (RECOURSE) for refractory mCRC. Label updated 2023 (SUNLIGHT) to include the trifluridine/tipiracil + bevacizumab combination.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 third-line+ option, both as monotherapy and in combination with bevacizumab (SUNLIGHT regimen).

trials.notes: Italian site (IRST Dino Amadori IRCCS). Not US-accessible.

next_steps: Bank as a 3L+ option, paired with bev under the SUNLIGHT regimen.
If the patient continues bevacizumab through multiple lines (no Avastin holiday between regimens), confirm cumulative dose tolerability with the prescribing physician.
notes: RECOURSE established 3L monotherapy; SUNLIGHT extended the label to the bev-combination.

regulatory_status: FDA label updated August 2023 to include the trifluridine/tipiracil + bevacizumab combination (SUNLIGHT). Both components individually approved.
guideline_status: NCCN category 1 third-line option after fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, and prior bev exposure.

manufacturer.notes: Same contacts as the monotherapy and bevacizumab rows.

payer_access_notes: Labeled combination; routinely covered. Cumulative bev exposure is the practical concern across multiple lines.
access_summary: Labeled 3L+ option that meaningfully extends OS over TAS-102 monotherapy (SUNLIGHT). Operational fit is 3L+, not now.
next_steps: Bank for the 3L+ sequence after FOLFIRI-bev and FOLFOX exposure.
notes: SUNLIGHT N Engl J Med 2023 anchors the combination evidence.

regulatory_status: Component drugs FDA-approved. Maintenance use is published regimen, not a labeled indication; routinely covered.
guideline_status: NCCN-listed maintenance option after first-line induction.

manufacturer.company: Genentech (bevacizumab); Genentech/Roche (Xeloda originally; capecitabine generic since 2013)

payer_access_notes: Routine coverage. Capecitabine PO is patient-friendly maintenance; the DPYD status (see target_validation row) gates the dose.
access_summary: Maintenance option after first-line induction. The patient is on FOLFIRI-bev with planned CRS-HIPEC, so the operational decision is whether to introduce a maintenance phase post-HIPEC rather than continue intermittent triplet.
next_steps: Decide on a post-HIPEC maintenance plan with the medical-oncology team. If maintenance is chosen, the cape-bev backbone is the operational standard.
Confirm DPYD genotype before starting capecitabine (target_validation has DPYD as essential).
notes: CAIRO3 is the registrational maintenance trial. Capecitabine became generic in 2013.

intervention_label: Cytoreductive surgery + HIPEC (mitomycin C or oxaliplatin)
regulatory_status: Surgical procedure plus off-label intraperitoneal use of approved chemo drugs. Not a labeled drug indication; HIPEC delivery is institution-specific protocol.
guideline_status: NCCN now lists CRS + HIPEC as a treatment option for selected mCRC patients with limited peritoneal disease (PCI < 20) at experienced centers (NCCN Colon Cancer v3.2026). ESMO 2025 retains a Category B recommendation for high-volume centers.

trials.title: EFFIPEC: CRS-HIPEC vs CRS alone in colorectal peritoneal metastases
trials.notes: Sweden + India sites only. Not US-accessible. Useful as the trial reading the field is watching for the HIPEC efficacy question.

trials.notes: University of Kentucky + University of Vermont. Open in the US.

trials.notes: Yale University; personalized HIPEC regimen selection.

manufacturer.company: Multiple HIPEC pump manufacturers (Belmont Medical, ThermoChem, RanD); chemo drugs are generic
manufacturer.notes: The procedure is institution-driven, not a single sponsor program. Mitomycin C generics (Mylan, Sandoz) and oxaliplatin generics dominate.

payer_access_notes: Medicare and most commercial payers cover CRS-HIPEC for selected CRC patients at experienced centers; PRODIGE-7 reduced enthusiasm for oxaliplatin HIPEC, and mitomycin C is the default agent in most US centers. Pre-authorization typically requires PCI documentation and a multidisciplinary tumor board record.
access_summary: Patient already has CRS-HIPEC planned. Access is about choosing a high-volume center and the HIPEC drug. Major US peritoneal surface malignancy centers include MSK, MD Anderson, Mayo Clinic (Rochester, Phoenix, Jacksonville), City of Hope, Wake Forest, UPMC (Pittsburgh's Sugarbaker network), Cleveland Clinic, and Moffitt. Mitomycin C is the post-PRODIGE-7 default; oxaliplatin HIPEC is largely off the table for CRC.
next_steps: Confirm the CRS-HIPEC center is high-volume (>20 cases/year) and uses mitomycin C as the default HIPEC agent; the post-PRODIGE-7 consensus is that oxaliplatin HIPEC adds toxicity without OS benefit.
Document peritoneal cancer index (PCI) and CC-0/CC-1 cytoreduction probability at the surgical consult.
Hold bevacizumab 4-6 weeks pre-op and resume 4-6 weeks post-op once the wound is healed.
Bracket the procedure with ctDNA (Signatera) per the target_validation row; baseline pre-op, day 30-60 post-op, then q8-12 weeks.
geographic_scope: United States — multiple high-volume peritoneal surface malignancy centers.
notes: PRODIGE-7 (Quenet et al. Lancet Oncol 2021) showed no OS benefit from oxaliplatin HIPEC. COLOPEC studied adjuvant HIPEC in T4/perforated colon; the EFFIPEC and HIPECT4 trials are the contemporary phase 3 question marks.

regulatory_status: Investigational in the US. PIPAC aerosolization equipment (Capnopen) is CE-marked in EU; not FDA-cleared as a system, so PIPAC is delivered under research protocols in the US.
guideline_status: Not yet in NCCN guidelines. ESMO acknowledges as a developing modality.

trials.title: PIPAC platform for peritoneal carcinomatosis (City of Hope, Mayo FL, Northwell)
trials.notes: Three US sites: City of Hope (Duarte CA), Mayo Clinic Jacksonville FL, Northwell Health Cancer Institute (Greenlawn NY). Operationally feasible if the patient's CRS-HIPEC is deferred.

trials.notes: Hong Kong only; not US-accessible.

next_steps: Reserve PIPAC for post-HIPEC peritoneal recurrence; not in scope while the upfront CRS-HIPEC is the plan.
If the team pivots to PIPAC instead of CRS-HIPEC, contact Thanh Dellinger at City of Hope (tdellinger@coh.org) — the most established US site.
geographic_scope: United States (3 trial sites) — investigational only.
notes: CRC-PIPAC and the PRECINCT registry support feasibility; survival evidence is registry-level. Sugarbaker network is rolling out PIPAC at additional US centers.

regulatory_status: Strategy combining approved drugs and standard surgical procedure. CAIRO6 is the registrational trial.
guideline_status: Multidisciplinary practice in high-volume centers; not a single-drug labeled indication.

trials.title: CAIRO6: perioperative systemic chemo + CRS-HIPEC vs CRS-HIPEC alone
trials.notes: Dutch / European trial; closed to new enrollment. Patient's pathway maps directly onto this schema.

trials.notes: Spanish / Maimónides Biomedical Research Institute. Not yet open.

access_summary: This is essentially the patient's pathway: induction FOLFIRI-bev, restaging, CRS-HIPEC, post-op systemic therapy. CAIRO6 is the closest published protocol template; new enrollment closed but the schema is operational at every high-volume US peritoneal-malignancy center.
next_steps: Coordinate the systemic-to-surgical-to-systemic transition with the medical oncology, surgical oncology, and HIPEC teams at the chosen center.
Use CAIRO6 as the published protocol template even though enrollment is closed.
notes: CAIRO6 design (FOLFOX or FOLFOXIRI ± bev before CRS-HIPEC) is the contemporary protocol reference.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved October 2024 (INAVO120) for PIK3CA-mutant, HR+, HER2-negative, endocrine-resistant advanced breast cancer in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant. EMA approval pending. No mCRC approval.
guideline_status: On-label only in breast. Not in NCCN Colon v3.2026. Off-label use in PIK3CA-mutant mCRC has no compendium support.

trials.notes: Roche umbrella mCRC platform with multiple biomarker-defined arms. PIK3CA M1043I sits within the PI3K-alpha activating-mutation cohort; KRAS A59T is unusual and may or may not flag a RAS-arm slot — sponsor confirmation is the gate.

trials.title: INAVO120: inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant (HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mut breast)
trials.notes: Registrational breast trial; closed to new enrollment. Not relevant to mCRC.

access_summary: Approved in PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer; off-label and not compendium-supported in mCRC. The clean access path for this patient is the Genentech INTRINSIC mCRC platform (NCT04929223), where PIK3CA M1043I would slot into the PI3K-alpha activating-mutation cohort and the sponsor covers the drug. Sponsor confirmation on A59T compatibility is the load-bearing gate.
next_steps: Email global-roche-genentech-trials@gene.com or call 888-662-6728 with the PIK3CA M1043I + KRAS A59T molecular profile to ask which INTRINSIC arm fits.

Confirm M1043I is treated as kinase-domain-activating by the sponsor's eligibility criteria (the canonical hotspots H1047R/E545K/E542K dominate the registry; M1043I is rarer and may require a sponsor exception).
If INTRINSIC is not accessible, do not pursue inavolisib off-label outside a trial — alpelisib has more mCRC-relevant trial signal.
notes: Selective inhibitor + degrader of mutant p110-alpha. INAVO120 anchored the breast approval. INTRINSIC is the umbrella mCRC platform.

regulatory_status: FDA-approved May 2019 (Piqray, SOLAR-1) for PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer in combination with fulvestrant. FDA-approved April 2022 (Vijoice) for PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS) in pediatric and adult patients. EMA-approved.
guideline_status: On-label only in breast and PROS. Not in NCCN Colon v3.2026. Off-label use in PIK3CA-mutant mCRC has no compendium support.

trials.title: ALCAP: alpelisib + capecitabine in PIK3CA-mut mCRC after 2 lines
trials.notes: Korean Cancer Study Group; Seoul, South Korea only. Not US-accessible. Trial registry has not been updated in months.

manufacturer.notes: Novartis Medical Information operates 1-888-NOW-NOVA. Patient Assistance Foundation handles uninsured; pre-approval Managed Access Program (MAP) handles compassionate / expanded access.
